institution: Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, New Delhi
citation: Institute of Clinical Microbiology and Immunology, Sir Ganga Ram Hospital. Clinical Microbiology Newsletter, Vol. 28, No. 2: % sensitivity in yeasts fungi (blood isolates), January to December 2021. New Delhi: Sir Ganga Ram Hospital; published December 2022.
reporting: Percent susceptible of yeasts isolated from blood, by species, for the whole hospital (one table, not split by OPD, ward and ICU), with the number of isolates tested per species in parentheses; amphotericin B, flucytosine, fluconazole, voriconazole, caspofungin and micafungin.
method: Antibiogram as per CLSI M39-A4 (printed "CLSI M-39A4E; 2014"), repeat isolates excluded; interpreted as per CLSI M60 (the table heading says 2020, the footnote 2018), and the C. albicans breakpoints were used where no species-specific breakpoints are available; C. glabrata voriconazole by an epidemiological cut-off of 0.25 µg/ml (CLSI gives no voriconazole criteria for C. glabrata); amphotericin B is reported as the percentage of isolates with MIC ≤1 µg/ml. The testing method (instrument or cards) is not named in this edition.
breakpoints: CLSI M60 (2020 in the table heading, 2018 in the footnote)

verification.note: The page 2 table was parsed from the PDF text layer (pdfplumber word positions; each cell assigned to its drug column by x position, the species label and the number tested read from the label), then every cell and every n was compared by eye with page 2 rendered at scale 4, first as the whole table band and then cut into two halves with the species column kept on both: no differences. Footnote marks and every cell printed with a symbol or text (NA, SDD, "-") were read on the image. The amphotericin B footnote was read at scale 8: the page prints "<" with an underline (read as ≤) where the text layer has "<". The other content (charts, filamentous fungi table and antifungal use chart on pages 2 and 3; pages 1 and 4 to 8) was identified from the text layer and the rendered pages only to describe it in excluded. A second reader re-read every cell and n against the page images on 2026-09-26 (see issues).

notes: Clinical Microbiology Newsletter of Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, Vol. 28, No. 2 (published December 2022), data January to December 2021, 8 pages. The No. 2 issue of each year carries the mycology, mycobacteriology, virology and serology results (the bacterial antibiogram is in No. 1). Recorded: the page 2 table "% Sensitivity in Yeasts Fungi* (Blood Isolates 2021)", one row per species with the number of isolates tested printed in parentheses (used as n, n_tested) and percent susceptible for amphotericin B, flucytosine, fluconazole, voriconazole, caspofungin and micafungin. The table covers blood isolates of all locations together and is not split by OPD, ward and ICU, so every row is set "all". The table heading says "interpreted as per CLSI M60 document, 2020" and the footnote "interpreted as per CLSI M60 document, 2018"; both are given in breakpoints. Other footnotes as in 2020: "*Antibiogram as per CLSI M-39A4E; 2014 (Rpt. isolates excluded)", no testing method named; C. albicans breakpoints where no species-specific breakpoints are available (noted on the cells concerned); ** amphotericin B as isolates with MIC ≤1 µg/ml (a "<" with an underline); # C. glabrata: fluconazole "100 SDD" (left out) and voriconazole by an epidemiological cut-off of 0.25 µg/ml. The paragraph under the table misprints two figures ("C. tropicalis (43 cases; 5%)", "C. parapsilosis (19 cases; 11. %)"). All eight species have organism keys. "Trichosporon asahii" keeps its printed name (Trichosporon key). The paragraph under the table gives the blood cases and share of each species, which can differ from the numbers tested; organism counts from the charts are not recorded (see excluded). The PDF has no direct link: sgrh.com serves the newsletters only by an HTTP POST from the Microbiology Newsletter issue selector on https://sgrh.com/en/publications (issue "December-2022"). The fungal issues are recorded as their own series (Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, fungal), so their editions trend with each other and are not taken for editions of the bacterial antibiogram published in the first issue of each volume.
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: every cell and every row n re-read from page 2 rendered at scale 4 (the table cut into two halves with the species column kept on both, footnotes cropped separately) and written down before comparing with the file; the seeded sample from sample_cells.py is part of this. All 47 cells and 8 n: 0 transcription errors, nothing corrected.

Confirmed: the heading says "CLSI M60 DOCUMENT, 2020" and the footnote "CLSI M60 document, 2018", both given in breakpoints; ** MIC ≤1 µg/ml (underlined "<"); C. glabrata fluconazole "100 SDD" left out with the right note. The intrinsic cell C. krusei fluconazole 0 is printed that way.
